sentences.text:
The present application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. seeks regular bail in case FIR No.
760/2021 under Sections 498A/304B of the IPC, registered at P.S. Mangolpuri.

2. The case of the prosecution as per the status report is as under:-
"It is submitted that On 18/06/21, a PCR call regarding hanging was received at Ps Mangolpuri vide DD No 69A.
On enquiry, it was found that one lady namely Laxmi Kumari Jha age 19 years hanged herself on the fan with the help of chunni at H No 187-188, Mangolpuri, New Delhi.
On further enquiry it was found that her marriage was solemnized on 14.12.2020 with Sajan.

Being the matter under 7 year of marriage,
information was given to SDM and mother of the deceased.
Mother of deceased who is a very poor lady arrived in Delhi on 23/06/21.

During course of investigation, PM report was collected and found ligature mark were present on neck.
Injury was also found on two fingers.
Accused was arrested on 25/06/21 on the instance of complainant.
Supplementary statement of complainant were recorded wherein she stated that with the help of villagers, she spent approx. Rs. 50,000/- in the said marriage.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Charge have been framed and case is on prosecution evidence.
Next date of hearing in this matter is 02/05/23 and mother of the deceased Anju Devi and neighbor Sumit are called for the same.
There are specific allegation of demand of dowry (Rs 5 lacs) by the accused in the statement given before SDM by the mother of deceased.
Beating and harassing allegations are also alleged against him.
Testimony of the prime witnesses is yet to be examined.
Accused is residing on rent in Delhi since a long and might be run away from trial.
Possibility of threatening of witnesses is also here as witnesses are very known to the accused."
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the applicant submits that the complainant/mother of the deceased has been examined as PW-1 before the learned Trial Court.

It is pointed out that during her examination-in-chief, the said witness did not support the case of the prosecution, however, in cross-examination by the learned APP, with the permission of the Court, she admitted that she filed the present complaint, as well as the allegations made therein.
4. It is further submitted that at one point during her cross-examination, the said witness stated that there was no demand of dowry from either the applicant or his parents.
It is further submitted that the present applicant has been in custody since 25.06.2021.
It is also pointed out that as per the nominal roll, the applicant was on interim bail from 18.04.2022 to 14.11.2022 and he did not misuse the liberty granted to him.

Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. It is pertinent to note that during examination-in-chief, mother of deceased/PW-1 has stated that marriage between the present applicant and the deceased was solemnized with the consent of family members as they liked each other.

The said witness, on cross-examination by learned APP has supported the case of the prosecution but has also admitted that in her cross-examination by the Sajan vs State on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37782456/

sentences.text: Further, another public witness/ PW-2 has not supported the case of the prosecution.

8. Be that as it may, the applicant has been in custody since 25.06.2021 and the main witness, i.e.,
mother of the deceased and other public witness/ PW-2 have been examined.
The trial is likely to take time.
The applicant was on interim bail from 18.04.2022 to 14.11.2022 and did not misuse the liberty granted to him.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the applicant in judicial custody any further.
9. In view thereof, the present application is allowed.

The applicant is directed to be released on bail,
on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety of like amount, to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court/Link Court, further subject to following conditions:
i.
The applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the learned Trial Court.
ii. The applicant shall intimate the learned Trial Court by way of an affidavit and to the Investigating Officer regarding any change in residential address.
This is a digitally signed order.

The applicant shall appear before the learned Trial Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
iv. The applicant is directed to give his mobile number to the Investigating Officer and keep it operational at all times.

v. The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly,
tamper with evidence or try to influence the witness in any manner.
10. The application is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
11. Pending application, if any, also stand disposed of.

12. Needless to state that nothing stated hereinabove is an opinion on the merits of the case.
13. Copy of the order be sent to the concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary information and compliance.
14. Order be uploaded on the website of this court forthwith.
